clue.text: As far as region of Mount Olivet

indicators.note: a region is a part of an area, so the answer is a part of the run of letters in these words

explanation.surface: Directions given for how far to travel on the Mount of Olives near Jerusalem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'region of' signals letters lying inside 'Mount Olivet': moUNT Olivet.
explanation.definitionFit: Unto is an archaic preposition meaning up to or until, the biblical way of saying how far.

parts.note: also means too, in addition
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: Someone credits a piece of ornamental craftwork to an artist named Heather.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a woman's name, but it is the plant, called LING in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Tooling is ornamental design pressed or carved into leather, as on book covers.

clue.text: Legal therefore to start and tout for trade

indicators.note: the piece meaning therefore is placed at the start, before the piece meaning legal

parts.note: so means therefore, as in 'and so'
licit means lawful or legal

explanation.surface: A trader asks whether it is lawful to begin hawking for business.
explanation.definitionFit: To solicit is to ask for custom, especially to approach people offering goods or services.

clue.text: Sort of nerve shown by secret agency infiltrating branch endlessly

indicators.note: infiltrating means one piece gets inside another, as agents get inside an organisation
endlessly means the last letter of the word for branch is dropped

parts.note: a stick is a small branch of a tree
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: Spies are shown to have the nerve to penetrate an endless branch office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts STICK to STIC, and 'infiltrating' puts CIA inside it: S-CIA-TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The sciatic nerve runs from the lower back down the leg, so sciatic names a particular nerve.

definitions.meaning: abandoned means deserted, gone away from
socialist means belonging to the political ...

explanation.surface: A left-wing politician has been deserted by colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left behind has been abandoned; politically the left wing is socialist.

clue.text: Enough for a talk with audience in a stately home?

parts.note: an amount sufficient for a chat is, read as a phrase, a chat's worth
a house is the audience in a theatre, as in 'a full house'

explanation.surface: Is there enough material to give a lecture to visitors at a grand country house?
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first part as 'chat's worth'. CHATSWORTH HOUSE is a famous stately home in Derbyshire, England, seat of the Dukes of Devonshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Chatsworth is a grand Derbyshire mansion, one of England's best-known country houses open to the public.

clue.text: Number of players on rugby field almost succeeded when hiding small items of kit

indicators.note: hiding means one piece keeps another concealed inside it
almost means the last letter of the number is left off

parts.words: Number of players on rugby field
parts.note: a rugby union match has fifteen a side, so thirty players on the field
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: A rugby team nearly wins while hiding small items of its kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts THIRTY to THIRT; add S for succeeded, and 'hiding' puts the S for small inside: T-S-HIRT-S.
explanation.definitionFit: T-shirts are short-sleeved tops, part of sports kit.

parts.note: read 'digital' as electronic rather than of fingers, and 'enlightenment' as a burst of light rather than understanding: a camera's light source

explanation.surface: A spiritual awakening brought on by computers.
explanation.definitionFit: An electronic flash is a camera's battery-powered light unit, so it supplies light by electronic means.

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea

explanation.surface: A railway line is shut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main line' looks like a railway term; 'main' is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To seal something is to close it up tight.

definitions.meaning: a female given name, short for Katherine
a shared fund built up by contributions

explanation.surface: A woman has been saving up her money.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitty is a woman's name, and a kitty is a pooled fund of money collected by a group.

clue.text: Old autocrat meets a revolutionary inside

indicators.note: inside means the answer sits within the run of letters of the next words

explanation.surface: A former dictator has a meeting with a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' signals letters lying within 'meets a revolutionary': meeTS A Revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was a Russian emperor with absolute power, the very type of an autocrat.

parts.note: the Mini is a famous small British car
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: Someone observes a little car on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a verb, but it is the musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is a musical note lasting half a semibreve, called a half note in America.

clue.text: Pose outside place in Croatian resort

indicators.note: outside means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: to sit is to pose for a portrait
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: Someone poses for a photo outside a spot in a Croatian holiday town.
explanation.definitionFit: Split is a port city and holiday destination on Croatia's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Giving instance of "fling" drunk knocked back gins with abandon

indicators.note: knocked back means the word for drunk is turned backwards, as a drink is thrown back

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard

indicators.note: with abandon means the letters are thrown about carelessly into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunkard downs gins recklessly, an example of a wild fling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' turns SOT into TOS, and 'with abandon' rearranges GINS into SING.
explanation.definitionFit: Tossing is throwing something, so the word is an example of flinging.

clue.text: Policeman with debts consisting of large amounts

parts.note: a cop is a policeman
IOUs are written promises to pay, so debts

explanation.surface: An officer with heavy debts that run to large sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Copious means plentiful or abundant, existing in great quantity.

clue.text: Plan performance to disrupt natural responses

indicators.note: to disrupt means one piece breaks into the middle of another

parts.note: tics are involuntary twitches, reflex responses
an act is a performance on stage

explanation.surface: A scheme to stage a show that will interrupt people's instinctive reactions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to disrupt' puts ACT inside TICS: T-ACT-ICS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactics are the methods planned to reach a goal, a scheme of action.

indicators.note: taking means the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: trad, short for traditional, means conservative in style
PPE is Philosophy, Politics and Economics, a famous Oxford degree

explanation.surface: A Tory politician who studied at Oxford has been found out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative' looks like the party; here it means TRAD. PPE is the Oxford degree many British politicians take.
explanation.definitionFit: Trapped means snared or caught with no way out.

clue.text: Cook, Irish father, in filthy living quarters

indicators.note: in means the two abbreviations go inside the word for the dirty dwelling

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty, the proverbially dirty home of pigs
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: An Irish priest does his cooking in squalid lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts IR and FR inside STY: ST-IR-FR-Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir-fry is to cook food quickly in hot oil while stirring, a verb for a way of cooking.

explanation.surface: Someone indicated something that turned out to be keen-edged.
explanation.definitionFit: To have pointed at something is to have indicated it; pointed also describes a tip that is sharp.

clue.text: Hooter turned up? Ask about gun going off

indicators.note: about means the word for ask goes round the other piece

parts.note: to pose a question is to ask it

indicators.note: going off means the letters explode into a new order, as a gun fires

explanation.surface: A gun goes off near someone asking about it, whose nose turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going off' rearranges GUN into UGN, and 'about' puts POSE round it: P-UGN-OSE. 'Hooter' is slang for a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A pug nose is short and upturned, like a pug dog's.

indicators.note: foreign means strange or altered, so the letters are put into an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: Don't upset the overseas nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to throw into disorder or unsettle the mind.

parts.note: A means one, as in 'a horse'

indicators.note: backed means the word for lawyers is put in reverse, as one backs a horse

parts.note: the Bar is the body of barristers

explanation.surface: A racehorse that one group of lawyers put money on.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arab is a famous breed of horse from the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Game to get quantity of wine and leave

parts.note: a bin is a wine-cellar rack, and the stock of wine it holds
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone plays a game to win wine and then departs.
explanation.walkthrough: BINGO is a numbers game played in British halls.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo is a game of chance in which called numbers are marked off on cards.

explanation.surface: Someone lets the tea scorch a little.
explanation.definitionFit: To char is to scorch the surface; char is also British slang for a cup of tea, from Chinese cha.

definitions.meaning: the title character of the Cole Porter song Miss ... Regrets
the elevator maker whose name is on many lift doors

explanation.surface: A regretful young woman thumbs a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss Otis Regrets is a Cole Porter song about a sorry lady; Otis is also the elevator company.

clue.text: Scot typically seeing officer after church

indicators.note: after means the officer comes after the church in the answer

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: A Scotsman meets an army officer after the church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots, like the Irish and Welsh, are Celtic peoples, so a Scot is an example of the type.

parts.note: read 'zero' as a decimal point plus no return, a nil rate of interest on savings, rather than boredom

explanation.surface: A loan or savings account paying no interest at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The point of no return is the stage past which turning back is impossible; read literally, a rate of nought yields nothing.

clue.text: Unpleasant woman at first abandoned by the French ruling family

indicators.note: at first means what is left of the woman goes at the front
abandoned by means the French word is dropped from the word for woman

parts.note: a lady is a woman
la is French for 'the'
nasty means unpleasant

explanation.surface: A nasty woman is first left by the French royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned by' takes LA out of LADY, leaving DY, which 'at first' puts before NASTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynasty is a line of hereditary rulers from one family.

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: wrong means the letters are put out of their right order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: An outdated gas meter is faulty and well off the mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Way out is slang for far beyond the normal, radical or outlandish.
